zh.question: 海水为什么会分层，又怎样上下交换、搬运热量？
zh.observe: 保留等体积A、B两份海水，分别改变A的温度与盐度，再让两种变化共同作用。播放或拖动同一剖面，比较相对密度次序；随后展开风、混合和上升流的联系。

academic.title: 密度差把温度与盐分连起来
academic.body: 在相同参考压力和本实验海水范围内，降温通常增密，增盐通常也增密，两种作用可以加强或抵消。真实海洋的表层与深层交换还依赖风、旋转、地形、混合与上升流。全球传送带是连接示意，不是每一滴水沿同一路线绕行的封闭管道。 密度参照采用历史EOS-80的海面形式及相应温标转换，限于本馆5—25°C、实用盐度30—38的对照；不求解完整海洋状态。

academic.title: 表层和深层有许多连接
academic.body: 风驱动许多表层海流；一些高纬海域的冷却与盐分变化参与深水形成。返回表层还涉及上升流和混合，不能把环流画成一滴水必走的封闭水管。旋转、岸线与海底地形也会改变路径。

academic.title: 密度比较能回答什么
academic.body: 本题在同一海面参考压力下比较密度，不能由两个读数直接算出下沉速度、真实深度、全球洋流或气候。连续水体和圆菱标记帮助追踪同一来源；虚线是解释边界，不是隔板。几何展开可回退，七个显示秒没有真实时间标定。颜色不代表实际温度，标记也不是分子或实测水团。

zh.misconception: 冷水不一定比任何暖水都密，盐分也要比较。海水抵达热带不会自动上浮；海洋也没有每一滴水必须走完的一圈。
zh.boundary: 密度使用本题温盐范围内的海面参考形式。图形解释相对分层和连接，不求解真实混合、流速或全球环流，不预测未来气候。昼夜、极光和宜居性另有专题入口；旧链接保留原观察，不再作为本题的默认学习路线。

narration.label: 先比同样大的一份水
narration.text: 两份一样大的海水，可以有不同的质量，也就有不同密度。冷暖和盐分都重要：冷一点的水如果也淡很多，结果还要一起比较。
narration.cue: 在连续水体剖面保留A圆点与B菱形，分别改变温度和盐度后再同时改变；播放、暂停并回退，寻找接近等密度的对照。虚线不是隔板。

narration.label: 海洋的上下有联系
narration.text: 风推动许多表层海流。有些地方的海水冷却、变咸，参与深水形成。混合和上升流又帮助深水返回。海洋有很多岔路，不是一根绕地球的水管。
narration.cue: 展开大洋联系示意，区分风驱表层、部分海域下沉与上升混合的返回机制，不承诺唯一闭合轨迹。

narration.label: 把两种变化放在一起
narration.text: 现在让海水同时变冷、变淡。两种作用可能互相抵消；要看同一次比较里的温度和盐分，不能只靠颜色判断。
narration.cue: 比较冷而较淡与暖而较咸的样本，保留A、B身份。

narration.label: 把海洋连接到别的发现
narration.text: 海洋和空气交换能量，也接收融水。要继续看冰川或大气，可以进入相邻专题；每一题都保留自己的问题和观察过程。
narration.cue: 从海洋链接进入冰川或大气，不把它们的进度合成同一只时钟。

en.question: Why does seawater form layers, and how does it exchange water and heat?
en.observe: Retain equal-volume samples A and B. Change A’s temperature and salinity separately and together, then play or scrub the same section to inspect density order. Expand the explanation of wind, mixing and upwelling.

academic.title: Density connects temperature and salt
academic.body: At the same reference pressure within this seawater experiment's range, cooling and increasing salinity usually increase density. Their effects can reinforce or counteract each other. Real exchange between surface and deep oceans also involves wind, rotation, topography, mixing and upwelling. The global conveyor illustrates connections, rather than a sealed pipe followed by every drop. Reference density uses the surface form of historical EOS-80 with the required temperature-scale conversion, limited here to 5-25 degrees Celsius and practical salinity 30-38, rather than a complete ocean state.

academic.title: Many connections join surface and deep water
academic.body: Wind drives many surface currents. Cooling and salinity changes in some high-latitude regions contribute to deep-water formation. Upwelling and mixing help return deeper water. Rotation, coasts and seafloor shape also affect pathways; circulation is not a closed pipe every water parcel must follow.

academic.title: What the density comparison establishes
academic.body: This study compares density at the same surface reference pressure. Two readouts do not calculate sinking speed, actual depth, global currents or climate. Continuous water regions and circle/diamond marks track origin; the dashed boundary is an explanation cue, not a divider. The geometry is reversible and seven display seconds have no physical time calibration. Colors do not encode actual temperature; marks are not molecules or measured ocean water masses.

en.misconception: Cold water is not necessarily denser than every warm sample: compare salinity too. Water does not automatically rise on reaching the tropics, and no parcel must complete one universal ocean circuit.
en.boundary: Density uses a surface-reference form within the study’s selected temperature and salinity range. Geometry explains relative layering and connections without solving real mixing, velocities or global circulation or predicting future climate. Day/night, auroras and habitability have separate entrances; explicit old links retain their observations without joining the default ocean route.

narration.label: Compare equal volumes of water
narration.text: Two equal-sized seawater samples can have different masses and therefore different densities. Temperature and salt both matter. If colder water is also much fresher, compare both changes together.
narration.cue: Retain A circles and B diamonds in the continuous water section. Vary temperature and salinity separately and together; play, pause and rewind, including a nearly equal-density case. The dashed boundary is not a divider.

narration.label: The surface and deep ocean connect
narration.text: Winds drive many surface currents. In some places, cooling and increasing salt contribute to deep-water formation. Mixing and upwelling help water return. The ocean has many branches, rather than one pipe wrapped around Earth.
narration.cue: Expand the ocean connections diagram. Distinguish wind-driven surface motion, sinking in some regions and return through upwelling and mixing, without promising a unique closed trajectory.

narration.label: Combine two changes
narration.text: Now make the water both colder and fresher. Their effects can oppose one another. Read temperature and salinity in the same comparison instead of judging by color alone.
narration.cue: Compare cold/fresh and warm/salty cases while retaining A and B.

narration.label: Connect the ocean to other questions
narration.text: The ocean exchanges energy with air and receives meltwater. Continue into the glacier or atmosphere study, each with its own question and observation process.
narration.cue: Follow a link to glaciers or atmosphere without combining their progress into one clock.
